property_summary: For any account address, the correct contract's maintenance(account) returns the stored per-product maintenance parameter (which can differ from UFixed18Lib.ONE), whereas the mutant always returns UFixed18Lib.ONE so there exists some account for which maintenance(account) != UFixed18Lib.ONE if the stored value is not ONE; the test fuzzes the stored maintenance value via initialize to find that difference.

For any initialized product info (any maintenance parameter), the reference contract's maintenance(account) returns the stored maintenance value; the mutant always returns ONE, so when the stored maintenance ≠ ONE the mutant's maintenance(account) differs — the test fuzzes the stored maintenance to find such a case.

For all initialization maintenance values, the reference contract's maintenance(account) returns the stored maintenance value (the Product's maintenance parameter); the mutant returns a constant ONE, so there exists some initialized maintenance value not equal to ONE that makes the mutant's maintenance(account) differ.

For any initialized product with maintenance parameter m, calling maintenance(account) must return that stored maintenance m; the mutant always returns ONE, so when the initialized maintenance m != ONE the mutant's maintenance(account) differs and the property is violated.

For any initialized product info, C.maintenance(account) must always return the product's stored maintenance parameter; the mutant always returns UFixed18Lib.ONE, so when the product was initialized with a maintenance value not equal to ONE the mutant will return a different value and thus violate the rule.

Reference contract always returns the stored current taker fee (pending updates do not affect takerFee()), whereas the mutant erroneously returns a pendingTakerFee when a pending update exists, causing takerFee() to sometimes differ.

For all states, the reference contract's takerFee() returns the stored effective taker fee (the committed _takerFee) regardless of pendingFeeUpdates(), whereas the mutant may instead return the pendingTakerFee when a pending update exists — so the property: takerFee() equals the committed stored taker fee when there is no committed change in storage, and the mutant will violate this for some pending update state.

For every input, the reference contract's takerFee() always returns the committed stored taker fee (the value in storage) regardless of any pending fee updates; the mutant wrongly returns the pendingTakerFee when a pending update exists, so for some fuzzed pending update value the mutant's takerFee() differs from the stored committed value.

For any pending fee state, the reference contract's takerFee() always returns the committed (stored) taker fee value; the mutant may instead return the pendingTakerFee when a pending update exists, so there exist inputs (a pending update state) where takerFee() differs.

For all inputs, the reference contract's takerFee() returns the committed stored taker fee (the value in storage) regardless of any pending fee updates; the mutant incorrectly returns a pendingTakerFee when a pending update exists, so there exist inputs (a pending pendingTakerFee flag/value) for which takerFee() differs.

For any contract state, C.positionFee() returns the exact stored pending position fee value; the mutant doubles the stored value (returns 2x), so there exists some stored non-zero fee where the mutant's return != reference.

For every stored position fee value, the reference contract's positionFee() returns exactly that stored value; the mutant returns double the stored value for some non-zero stored fees, so there exists inputs (a non-zero position fee set during initialization) where positionFee() differs.

For any product initialized with a positionFee value x, the reference contract's positionFee() returns x; the mutant returns 2*x for some x (non-zero), so there exists an initialization (fuzzed positionFee) where the returned value differs.

For any initialized product, C.positionFee() returns the stored single position fee value; the mutant returns twice that stored value for some initialized non-zero positionFee, so there exists an initialization (fuzzed positionFee) where C.positionFee() != mutant.positionFee().

For every initialized product, C.positionFee() returns the stored _positionFee value; the mutant returns double that value for some non-zero initialized positionFee, so there exists an initialization (fuzzed positionFee) where the returned value differs.

For any deployed product contract, the stored maker limit (what makerLimit() returns) equals the value previously initialized/stored; the mutant that hardcodes makerLimit() to UFixed18Lib.ONE will return a different value for any initialization where the stored makerLimit != ONE, causing the property to fail for such inputs.

For any fuzzed storedMakerLimit (initialized via calling initialize with ProductInfo.makerLimit), the deployed reference C returns that storedMakerLimit from makerLimit(); the mutant that hardcodes makerLimit() to UFixed18Lib.ONE will differ whenever the initialized storedMakerLimit != ONE, so there exists fuzz inputs that make the outputs differ.

For any initialized product info makerLimit value x, the deployed (reference) contract returns makerLimit()==x; the mutant that hardcodes makerLimit() to ONE will differ for any fuzzed x != ONE (so there exist inputs where the outputs diverge).

For any UFixed18 value `x` used to initialize C via ProductInfo.makerLimit, the reference contract returns makerLimit()==x (reads stored value); the mutant that hardcodes makerLimit() to UFixed18Lib.ONE will differ whenever x != ONE (so there exist fuzz inputs that make the outputs diverge).

For every UFixed18 value used to initialize C, the deployed (reference) contract's makerLimit() returns that stored value; the mutant that hardcodes makerLimit() to ONE will for some fuzzed initialization value (any value != ONE) return a different value, so there exists an input where outputs differ.

For any caller that is the product owner (controller().owner(coordinatorId)), calling updateMaintenance(newMaintenance) always succeeds (does not revert) on the reference contract; the mutant errone requires msg.sender == controller().owner() (different owner lookup) and thus can revert for some callers (fuzzer will find one).
